intro: Before you stands the Hüdavend Hatun Tomb, a tomb in Niğde province, built in 1312. This octagonal tomb was raised for a daughter of the Seljuk sultan Kilij Arslan IV. Look closely at its carving: angels, double-headed eagles and human faces, combined in a way found nowhere else in Anatolia.
history: The octagonal tomb at Niğde was built in 1312 for Hüdavend Hatun, daughter of the Seljuk sultan Kilij Arslan IV. Its angels, double-headed eagles and human faces appear together like this on no other building in Anatolia. And the carving on its drum pushes at the very limits of figural work in Islamic art.
highlights: As you walk around it, don't miss the octagonal shaft, the angel figures, the double-headed eagles and the muqarnas drum.
facts: Did you know? It has been argued that the angels represent Hüdavend Hatun herself — though no reading is settled. What is certain is that its angels, double-headed eagles and human faces appear in this combination on no other building in Anatolia.
outro: This brings our tour of the Hüdavend Hatun Tomb to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. Take one last look at those carved faces before you go. Enjoy your visit.
